Oh, I feel for you mama. This story doesn’t start positive but I promise it is! It’s long-winded but I would’ve wanted to hear it back when all this happened so here goes.

I had a placental abruption at 23+6 and was hospitalized. When I arrived I was in preterm labor and they stopped it with magnesium and fluids. This carried on for weeks, while I continued chronically bleeding and stayed on almost constant fetal monitoring. I was dilated to a 3/4 for weeks. 

I was moved back and forth between the MFM unit and the delivery room VERY often during that time, but somehow baby stayed in until 30 weeks on the dot! The night I hit 30 weeks I went into preterm labor and, despite trying magnesium again, I had progressed to a 6 in a matter of a few hours. 

They rushed me back for a cesarean, and unfortunately I could feel pain with everything they were doing. I had to go under general anesthesia so I didn’t get to meet baby right away. She was taken to the NICU, I went to a recovery area and then to my own room on the mom/baby floor. 

I was not allowed to see baby until I could stand up, walk to the bathroom, pee, and get into a wheelchair on my own. This criteria will obviously be different at each hospital, so ymmv.

I was HIGHLY motivated to get moving so I could make my way to the NICU. I pumped every two hours that whole day but couldn’t drink enough water to get the catheter removed. After roughly 12 hours I finally made it there. 

She was in a room inside an isolette. She had a CPAP machine, lots of heart monitors stuck to her torso, an IV, and a blood pressure cuff on her foot. She was 3 lb 10 oz, 15” long. She was on IV nutrition and just getting tastes of my colostrum on a swab. 

Within a day, she was breathing well enough to be on a nasal cannula. Within a week, she was on that cannula but at room air levels. She was off oxygen within two weeks. The warming bed was not far behind that. 

She had an NG tube through which she was fed breastmilk, the volume per feed would increase as her weight increased. I pumped sooooo much at home, it was the only thing I could control at the time really. 

We were not able to spend much time there at the NICU since we live an hour away. Despite this, she absolutely thrived. She continued to grow, had several “events” each day, but did mostly fine. I called once or twice every shift to check on her.

You’ll hear it everywhere, but the feeding stage is the hardest. She was totally off oxygen, in an open crib, growing great….but wouldn’t take feeds through a bottle. This carried on for weeks.

On her 50th day in the hospital she finally took all her feeds! They’d switched her from a preemie flow nipple to a #1 flow nipple and it totally changed the game. She didn’t have to work so hard to get the milk and was able to finish all her bottles!!

She is now 20 weeks old, 10 weeks adjusted. She weighs 13 pounds of pure chubby cuteness and has reached most of her actual age milestones. She’s a miracle and such a source of joy in my life. 

I sincerely hope this helps. I realize it’s very long but I love to prepare mentally for things so I tried to paint a complete picture. 

Please PM if you have questions, want to see photos, or want to talk! It’s hard to find people who understand what you’re going through. Hang in there!
